text_blocks.snippet: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev invented the first recognizable periodic table in 1869.

list.snippet: The Date: Mendeleev presented his arrangement to the Russian Chemical Society on March 6, 1869.
How It Worked: He organized the 63 elements known at the time by their atomic weight and chemical properties.
The Genius: He left blank spaces in his table and correctly predicted the existence and properties of undiscovered elements, such as gallium, germanium, and scandium.
Other Contributors: German chemist Lothar Meyer independently created a very similar table around the same time (1870), but Mendeleev is most famous for predicting new elements.
Modern Updates: Early tables were based on atomic weight, but in the early 20th century, scientists reorganized the table using atomic numbers (the number of protons).
